##### **1.2 Standard LP Augmentation and Initial Simplex Tableau Construction** Executing the simplex method computationally requires casting a linear program into standard equality form and tabulating the resulting linear system. **Standard LP augmentation** is the systematic algebraic conversion of inequality constraints into linear equalities by introducing auxiliary non-negative variables, accompanied by rewriting the objective relation as a single homogeneous zero-sum equation. ###### **1.2.1 Constraint Augmentation via Slack Variables** When constraints are expressed as less-than-or-equal-to inequalities ($\le$), each inequality represents an upper bound on resource utilization. A **slack variable** $s_i \ge 0$ is added to the left-hand side of the $i$-th constraint to absorb the difference between the actual resource consumption and the maximum allowable capacity: $$\sum_{j=1}^n a_{ij} x_j \le b_i \iff \sum_{j=1}^n a_{ij} x_j + s_i = b_i, \quad s_i \ge 0$$ where $b_i \ge 0$ constitutes the non-negative right-hand-side requirement. Each introduced slack variable possesses a cost coefficient of zero in the original objective function, ensuring that unused resource quantities do not directly alter the calculated objective value $z$. ###### **1.2.2 Homogeneous Objective Equation Reformulation** The linear objective function $\max z = \sum_{j=1}^n c_j x_j + \sum_{i=1}^m 0 s_i$ is treated algebraically as an additional linear equation. To integrate it directly into an elimination system, all decision and slack variable terms are shifted to the left-hand side, establishing the **homogeneous objective form**: $$z - \sum_{j=1}^n c_j x_j - \sum_{i=1}^m 0 s_i = 0$$ In this form, each decision variable $x_j$ appears with coefficient $-c_j$, and the right-hand-side constant equals zero at the starting baseline. ###### **1.2.3 Basic and Nonbasic Variable Partitioning** For an augmented linear system containing $m$ functional equality constraints and $n + m$ total variables (decision variables plus slacks), there are more unknowns than linearly independent equations. The simplex framework partitions the variables into two distinct subsets: * **Nonbasic variables:** A subset of $(n + m) - m = n$ variables assigned an exact numerical value of zero. At the initial construction, the original decision variables ($x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n$) are designated as nonbasic, representing the coordinate origin. * **Basic variables:** A subset of $m$ variables whose values are uniquely resolved from the constraint equations once the nonbasic variables are set to zero. At initialization, each constraint equation contains exactly one isolated slack variable with a coefficient of $+1$, allowing the set of slack variables ($s_1, s_2, \dots, s_m$) to serve as the initial **basis**. Setting the nonbasic variables to zero simplifies the augmented system $\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x} + \mathbf{I}\mathbf{s} = \mathbf{b}$ to $\mathbf{I}\mathbf{s} = \mathbf{b}$, immediately yielding the **initial basic feasible solution (BFS)**: $$\mathbf{s} = \mathbf{b} \ge \mathbf{0}, \quad \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{0}, \quad z = 0$$ ```{mermaid} %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'Helvetica', 'primaryColor': '#e8f4f8', 'primaryTextColor': '#1f2d3d', 'primaryBorderColor': '#355c7d', 'lineColor': '#355c7d', 'secondaryColor': '#d6eef5', 'tertiaryColor': '#fff3cd', 'background': '#ffffff', 'mainBkg': '#e8f4f8', 'secondBkg': '#d6eef5', 'tertiaryBkg': '#fff3cd', 'clusterBkg': '#f9fbfd', 'clusterBorder': '#355c7d', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#ffffff' }}}%% %%| fig-cap: "Standard LP augmentation and initial simplex tableau setup pipeline" %%| fig-width: 7 %%| fig-height: 4 flowchart TB A["Original Model

Shift z terms to LHS"] C --> D["Partition Variables
Nonbasic to zero, slacks basic"] D --> E["Initial Simplex Tableau
Read starting BFS from RHS"] ``` ###### **1.2.4 Canonical Simplex Tableau Structure and Concrete Formulation** The full augmented system of linear equations is arranged into a standardized compact matrix structure called the **simplex tableau**. The canonical tableau organizes coefficients across distinct functional columns: 1. **Basic column:** Lists the current basic variables corresponding to each constraint row, with the top row reserved for the objective variable $z$. 2. **$z$-column:** Displays the coefficients of the objective variable $z$ (identically $1$ in the $z$-row and $0$ in all constraint rows). 3. **Variable columns:** Contains the structural constraint coefficients under both decision variables ($x_j$) and slack variables ($s_i$). The basic slack variables form an $m \times m$ identity matrix $\mathbf{I}$. 4. **Solution (RHS) column:** Holds the constant terms $b_i$, from which the numerical values of the basic variables and the objective $z$ are read directly. Consider the Tatar-Paint problem with decision variables $x_1$ and $x_2$ and four operational restrictions: $$\begin{aligned} \text{Maximize } & z = 5x_1 + 4x_2 \\ \text{Subject to } & 6x_1 + 4x_2 \le 24 && \text{(Raw material M1)} \\ & x_1 + 2x_2 \le 6 && \text{(Raw material M2)} \\ & -x_1 + x_2 \le 1 && \text{(Market limit)} \\ & x_2 \le 2 && \text{(Demand limit)} \\ & x_1, x_2 \ge 0 \end{aligned}$$ Introducing slack variables $s_1, s_2, s_3, s_4 \ge 0$ converts the inequalities into equalities, and rearranging the objective relation produces: $$\begin{aligned} z - 5x_1 - 4x_2 - 0s_1 - 0s_2 - 0s_3 - 0s_4 &= 0 \\ 6x_1 + 4x_2 + s_1 &= 24 \\ x_1 + 2x_2 + s_2 &= 6 \\ -x_1 + x_2 + s_3 &= 1 \\ x_2 + s_4 &= 2 \end{aligned}$$ Setting the $n = 2$ nonbasic variables to zero ($x_1 = 0, x_2 = 0$) isolates the $m = 4$ basic variables as $s_1 = 24$, $s_2 = 6$, $s_3 = 1$, and $s_4 = 2$, yielding $z = 0$. This configuration is tabulated into the initial simplex tableau: | Basic | $z$ | $x_1$ | $x_2$ | $s_1$ | $s_2$ | $s_3$ | $s_4$ | Sol. | Row Identifier | | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- | | $z$ | 1 | -5 | -4 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | $z$-row | | $s_1$ | 0 | 6 | 4 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 24 | $s_1$-row | | $s_2$ | 0 | 1 | 2 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 6 | $s_2$-row | | $s_3$ | 0 | -1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 1 | $s_3$-row | | $s_4$ | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 2 | $s_4$-row | The identity matrix embedded under columns $s_1, s_2, s_3, s_4$ explicitly mirrors the basis. The rightmost Solution column immediately provides the initial basic feasible coordinate vector $(x_1, x_2, s_1, s_2, s_3, s_4) = (0, 0, 24, 6, 1, 2)$ at profit level $z = 0$.
